options.systemMessage:
# Overview
You are an AI agent that writes a single concise, inspiring LinkedIn post for an entrepreneur audience, based on the reference articles provided.

# Context
- You will receive a topic and one or more reference articles on that topic.
- Your job is to synthesize the key ideas into one short, professional LinkedIn post.
- The post should be optimized for engagement using relevant hashtags and light emoji use.

# Instructions
1. Read all provided articles and identify the core themes, trends, or insights.
2. Find the common thread or single overarching message across them.
3. Write one LinkedIn post, maximum 700 characters, that blends the main insight into a unified, inspiring message.
4. Add 2-4 relevant hashtags related to the post topic and entrepreneur interests. Hashtags must have no space after the # symbol (e.g. #AI, not # AI).
5. Add 1-3 tasteful emojis if they genuinely add value — never more, never purely decorative.
6. Never quote or directly reference the source articles by name. Synthesize ideas in your own words.
7. Ground every claim in what the articles actually say. Do not invent statistics, studies, or facts not present in the source material.
8. If fewer than 3 articles are provided, write the post from whatever is available rather than referencing a missing article.

# Example
Input: articles on AI in startups, bootstrapping, and the rise of solopreneurs.
Output:
"From AI copilots to lean bootstrapping, the age of the solopreneur is here.
Entrepreneurs are rewriting the rules — scaling smarter, faster, and with less.
Embrace the shift. The tools are here. The future is solo-powered.
#Entrepreneurship #AI #Bootstrapping #FutureOfWork"

# Output format
Output ONLY the final LinkedIn post text. No preamble, no explanation, no meta-commentary, no labels like "Post:" before it.

# Final notes
- The post must always be original phrasing, never copied from the source articles.
- Avoid technical jargon or niche terms — keep it accessible to a general entrepreneur audience.
- Prioritize clarity, brevity, and emotional resonance over completeness.

options.systemMessage:
# Overview
You are an AI agent that converts a finished LinkedIn post into a single detailed image-generation prompt for an AI image model. The image should look like a modern tech/SaaS marketing graphic, not a photograph.

# Context
- You will receive the topic and the final LinkedIn post text.
- Your output is not the LinkedIn post — it is a visual concept and generation parameters for an image model.
- The target style is flat or isometric illustration, or a stylized 3D-rendered character/icon composition — clean, modern, tech-forward. Think SaaS product marketing graphics, not editorial photography.

# Instructions
1. Read the post closely and find one literal phrase or vivid image already suggested by its own language (e.g. "breaking past screens," "building the future," "moving intelligence into the physical world"). Anchor the entire visual concept around that phrase — do not invent a generic metaphor unrelated to the post's actual wording.
2. Extract one short, punchy headline (3-6 words) that captures the post's core message — this will appear as bold text in the image. Instruct the model to render this text exactly as written, verbatim.
3. Design the scene in two layers: a foreground element (the central illustrated subject or icon composition) and a background/supporting element that visually represents the "physical," "system," or "outcome" side of the concept.
4. Explicitly state, in one short clause, what the juxtaposition of foreground and background is meant to convey — the same way a director's note would ("this highlights..." / "symbolizing..."). This is written into the prompt itself, not left implicit.
5. Identify 2-4 short supporting concepts or keywords related to the topic that can appear as small icon+label elements in the layout.
6. Specify a bold, modern color palette: a 2-3 color gradient or contrast scheme appropriate to a professional tech brand.
7. Specify atmosphere and lighting in one phrase (e.g. "optimistic and dynamic, warm light blending into cool futuristic blues") to give the image mood, not just flat lighting.
8. Specify layout: clean negative space, the headline prominent and legible, icon elements arranged in a grid or scattered supporting layout, generous margins.
9. Do NOT depict real, photographed people or faces — use stylized illustrated characters, silhouettes, or abstract figures only.
10. Do NOT include any specific company name, logo, website URL, or phone number.
11. Do NOT fabricate statistics or claims in the headline — it must be a direct restatement of the post's core message.
12. Write the prompt with as much descriptive detail as the concept genuinely needs — foreground, background, symbolic meaning, palette, atmosphere, and layout should each get real description rather than being compressed into a single clause. Do not pad with filler, but do not artificially shorten either.

# Example
Post: a message about AI moving beyond screens and software into physical systems like factories and machines, urging entrepreneurs to guide it with purpose.

Output:
"Promt" : "Image 1": "Modern isometric tech illustration, bold headline text 'AI Moves Beyond Screens' in clean white sans-serif at top, foreground: a stylized glowing digital robotic arm dissolving from a data-lattice pattern into solid polished metal, background: an illustrated factory floor with smart machines, this transition symbolizes intelligence crossing from software into the physical world, small icon labels scattered around: 'Efficiency', 'Smart Systems', 'Purpose', optimistic dynamic mood with warm light blending into futuristic blue tones, deep blue-to-violet gradient background, generous negative space, clean modern SaaS marketing style, no real people, no logos"
 "aspect_ratio": "4:5"
 "resolution": "1K"
"output_format": "png"

parameters.content: # LinkedIn Post Agent — Workflow Documentation & Setup Guide

# What This Workflow Does

Every day (or whenever you run it manually), this workflow picks up a topic from a Google Sheet, researches the latest news on that topic, writes a LinkedIn post about it, generates a matching graphic, sends both to you on Telegram for approval, and — once you approve — publishes the post to LinkedIn and marks the row as done. If you reject it, it automatically tries again with a fresh version.

In short: Topic → Research → Write Post → Generate Image → Send for Approval → Publish → Log.

# How the Whole Flow Works 
1. You (or a daily schedule) start the workflow.
2. It opens your "LinkedIn Post" Google Sheet and grabs the first row marked Status: To Do.
3. It searches the web for the 3 most recent news articles on that row's topic.
4. An AI agent reads those articles and writes one polished LinkedIn post (under 700 characters, with hashtags and a couple of emojis).
5. A second AI agent turns that post into a detailed image generation prompt — describing a headline, visual concept, colors, and mood for a matching graphic.
6. That prompt is sent to an image-generation API (kie.ai / "nano-banana-pro"). The workflow checks in periodically until the image is ready.
7. The finished image is downloaded, and the post text + image are sent to you on Telegram with Approve / Disapprove buttons.
8. If you approve: the sheet row is updated to Status "Created" with the final post text and image link, and the post is published to LinkedIn.
9. If you disapprove: the workflow loops back to the research step and generates a brand-new post and image for the same topic, then asks you again.

# When clicking 'Execute workflow' (Manual Trigger) 
Lets you run the workflow on demand for testing. Node type: manualTrigger.

# Schedule Trigger 
Runs the workflow automatically every day at 19:00 (7 PM). Node type: scheduleTrigger, interval: daily, triggerAtHour: 19.

# Get row(s) in sheet 
Opens the "LinkedIn Post" Google Sheet and pulls the row(s) where the Status column equals "To Do." This is the topic the workflow will write about. Node type: googleSheets, operation: read with filter Status = To Do, credential: Google Sheets OAuth2.

# Search (Tavily) 
Searches the web for "Latest developments in [Topic] 2026" and returns the top 3 news results (advanced search depth). This is the raw material the AI will write from. Node type: @tavily/n8n-nodes-tavily.tavily, topic: news, max_results: 3, credential: Tavily API.

# Generate Text AI Agent 
An AI agent (GPT-4.1) reads the topic and the 3 articles and writes a single LinkedIn post — max 700 characters, 2-4 relevant hashtags, 1-3 tasteful emojis, no direct quoting of sources, no invented facts. Output is plain text only. Node type: @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent, model: GPT-4.1 via "OpenAI Chat Model1," connected LLM credential: OpenAI API.

# OpenAI Chat Model
The brain behind the agent that 
reads the articles and writes a
single LinkedIn post

# Generate Prompt AI Agent
 A second AI agent (GPT-4.1) reads the finished LinkedIn post and converts it into a detailed image-generation brief: a punchy headline, foreground/background visual concept, symbolic meaning, color palette, mood, and layout — styled like a modern SaaS marketing graphic. Output is forced into strict JSON via the Structured Output Parser below it. Node type: @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent, model: GPT-4.1 via "OpenAI Chat Model," output parser attached.

# OpenAI Chat Model
The brain behind the Prompt agent that 
generates the prompt for the image 
for the LinkedIn Post

# Set Text For Post 
Takes the AI's raw output and stores it cleanly as a field called Post Text, so later nodes (image prompt, Telegram, Sheet update) can reference it consistently. Node type: set.

# Structured Output Parser 
Forces the AI's response into 
a fixed JSON shape
 (Image 1, aspect_ratio, resolution, output_format) 
so the next node can use it reliably 
instead of parsing free text. 
Node type: outputParserStructured.

# Send Image Request {HTTP Request}
Sends the image prompt to the kie.ai image API (model: nano-banana-pro) to start generating the graphic. Returns a taskId used to check progress. Node type: httpRequest, method: POST, endpoint: api.kie.ai/api/v1/jobs/createTask.

# Wait 
Pauses briefly before checking whether the image is ready. Node type: wait.

# Get Image1 
Checks the status of the image generation job using the taskId. Node type: httpRequest, endpoint: api.kie.ai/api/v1/jobs/recordInfo.

# Switch6
Reads the job's status and routes accordingly:
1. success → image is ready, continue
2. failed → stop this branch (does nothing further)
3. waiting / queuing / generating → loop back to Wait, then check again Node type: switch, checks data.state.

# Code in JavaScript6 
Once the image is ready, this pulls the actual image file URL out of the API's nested response and extracts a few extra details (task ID, model, credits used, time taken). Node type: code (JavaScript).

# Download Image1 
Downloads the actual image file from that URL as binary data, so it can be sent to Telegram or LinkedIn. Node type: httpRequest.

# Merge 
Combines the post text (from "Set Text For Post") with the downloaded image (from "Download Image1") into one item, matched by position, so everything travels together from here on. Node type: merge, mode: combine by position.

# Send a photo message 
Sends the generated image to your Telegram chat. Node type: telegram, operation: sendPhoto.

# Send message and wait for response 
Sends the post text to the same Telegram chat with Approve/Disapprove buttons and pauses the workflow until you respond. Node type: telegram, operation: sendAndWait, approval type: double (two buttons).

# Switch 
Reads your Telegram response (approved: true/false) and routes:

1. Approved → Update row in sheet → publish
2. Disapproved → Limit → loop back to Search (start over on the same topic) Node type: switch, checks data.approved.

# Update row in sheet 
Updates the original Google Sheet row: sets Status to "Created", and writes in the final Text Post Content and Image Post URL. Matches the correct row using the Topic column. Node type: googleSheets, operation: update.

# Limit 
Passes through only the first item to prevent duplicate/extra runs before looping back into the Search node to regenerate a new post and image. Node type: limit.

# Create a post 
Publishes the approved post to LinkedIn. Node type: linkedIn

# Setup Guide
## 1. Google Sheet

Create/confirm a Google Sheet called "LinkedIn Post" with these exact column headers (note the trailing space on "Topic "):

Topic	Status	Text Post Content	Image Post URL
Add a row for each topic you want a post about, with Status = To Do.
The workflow will change Status to Created automatically once a post is approved and published.
## 2. Connect Your Accounts (Credentials)

In n8n, go to Credentials and connect the following — each corresponding node will show a red warning icon until this is done:

Service	Used By	What You Need
Google Sheets	Get row(s) in sheet, Update row in sheet	Google account OAuth login
Tavily	Search	Tavily API key (from tavily.com)
OpenAI	Generate Text AI Agent, Generate Prompt AI Agent	OpenAI API key
kie.ai	Send Image Request, Get Image1	kie.ai API key (see fix below — should be moved into a proper credential rather than typed into the node)
Telegram	Send a photo message, Send message and wait for response	Telegram Bot token + your chat ID
LinkedIn	Create a post	LinkedIn OAuth login (connect your LinkedIn account)
## 3. Test It Manually First

Click "Execute workflow" on the Manual Trigger node to run one full cycle end-to-end. Watch for:

A Telegram message with an image and Approve/Disapprove buttons.
Tapping Approve should update the Google Sheet and publish to LinkedIn.
Tapping Disapprove should trigger a fresh post + image for the same topic, and ask you again.
## 4. Turn On the Daily Schedule

Once testing looks good, activate the workflow (toggle it "Active" in n8n). It will then automatically run every day at 7:00 PM and pick up the next "To Do" row.

5. Ongoing Use
Add new topics to the sheet anytime with Status = "To Do."
Approve or reject posts via Telegram as they come in.
Check the sheet's Status column to see what's been published.
